original_question: With discrepancy defined by disc(A) = inf_{x in {+1,-1}^n} ||Ax||_infinity for A in {+1,-1}^{n x n}, is it true that limsup_{n->infinity} sup_{A in {+1,-1}^{n x n}} (1/sqrt(n)) * disc(A) > 1?
target_in_paper: Entry 6 (“Did just a couple of deviations suffice all along?”), specifically Conjecture 12, with immediate motivating context from Open Problem 11.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s intended asymptotic question almost exactly: it uses the same discrepancy definition disc(A) = inf_{x∈{±1}^n} ||Ax||∞, the same class of matrices A∈{±1}^{n×n}, the same normalization by 1/√n, and the same threshold statement limsup > 1. In substance, it matches Conjecture 12 rather than the broader preceding Open Problem 11.
missing_details: State explicitly that n ranges over positive integers, i.e. n ∈ ℕ.
State explicitly that A is a real n×n sign matrix, meaning every entry of A is ±1; no symmetry, orthogonality, or other structural assumption is imposed.
State explicitly that x ranges over sign vectors x ∈ {±1}^n of the same dimension as A.
Specify that ||·||∞ is the usual ℓ∞-norm on ℝ^n.

If the question is meant to be fully paper-faithful, note that the paper first poses the broader Open Problem 11 asking for the exact value of sup_{n∈ℕ} sup_{A∈{±1}^{n×n}} n^{-1/2} disc(A), and then records your draft’s statement as the weaker asymptotic Conjecture 12.

For stand-alone clarity, say that the conjecture is motivated by the absence of any known infinite family of ±1 matrices with normalized discrepancy strictly larger than 1, although this is motivation rather than part of the formal statement.
refined_question: For each positive integer n and each real sign matrix A ∈ {±1}^{n×n}, define its discrepancy by disc(A) := inf_{x∈{±1}^n} ||Ax||∞, where ||·||∞ is the usual ℓ∞-norm on ℝ^n. Is it true that limsup_{n→∞} sup_{A∈{±1}^{n×n}} n^{-1/2} disc(A) > 1?
justification: The draft is aiming at Entry 6, not Entry 1: after defining disc(A), the paper first asks Open Problem 11 for the exact value of sup_{n∈ℕ} sup_{A∈{±1}^{n×n}} n^{-1/2} disc(A), and then immediately states Conjecture 12 as the asymptotic claim limsup_{n→∞} sup_{A∈{±1}^{n×n}} n^{-1/2} disc(A) > 1 (Entry 6, p. 8). Your draft reproduces that latter conjecture almost verbatim. The nearby context also explains why this asymptotic formulation is singled out: the author says that, to the best of his knowledge, no infinite family is known with normalized discrepancy strictly larger than 1, and later notes that Conjecture 13 about odd Sylvester Hadamard matrices would imply Conjecture 12 (Entry 6, p. 9). Since the paper does not present an explicit equivalence for Conjecture 12, there is no paper-certified alternate formulation to report.
